description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on constructor overloading in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
new maths(20, 40) matches (int, int) and prints 20 + 40 = 60. 12.0 is a double, so new maths(12.0, 12) matches (double, int) and prints 12.0 * 12 = 144.

Output:

60
144

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
new maths(6) uses the one-parameter constructor: length = 6 + 1 = 7. new maths(6, 2) uses the two-parameter constructor: length = 6 + 2 = 8. breadth is never set (stays 0) and is not printed.

Output:

7
8

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Constructors run in the order of the new expressions. new maths(4) prints constructor 2: 6. Then new maths() prints constructor 1 :

Output:

constructor 2: 6
constructor 1 :

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
:base(x) runs the base constructor first, which prints " hello: ", then the derived constructor prints "bye". The argument 12 is stored in i but is not written to the console.

Output:

 hello: 
bye

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
Derived constructors call :base(...) first, so the chain is maths, then maths1, then maths2. Each constructor overwrites its parameter before printing: 12 * 12 = 144, then 13 + 13 = 26, then 24 / 6 = 4. The 10 passed from Main is never used in the printed expressions.

Output:

144
26
4

questions.question: Which keyword is used to refer baseclass constructor to subclass constructor?
questions.explanation: A derived constructor calls a base constructor with : base(...). this(...) calls another constructor of the same class. C# has no extend keyword for this.

questions.question: When we call a constructor method among different given constructors. We match the suitable constructor by matching the name of constructor first, then the number and then the type of parameters to decide which constructor is to be overloaded. The process is also known as?
questions.explanation: Choosing among overloaded constructors by argument count and types is compile-time (static) polymorphism, also called overload resolution. It is not overriding, which is a runtime dispatch of virtual methods.

questions.question: Correct statement about constructor overloading in C# is?

options.text: Overloaded constructors have the same name as the class
Overloaded constructors cannot use optional arguments
Overloaded constructors may differ in parameter types and/or in the number of parameters

questions.explanation: Overloads are distinguished by signature (parameter count and types). Constructors are named after the class, so a is also true, but b is false: constructors may use optional parameters. Therefore d is false. c is the statement that actually describes overloading.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation:
The base constructor runs first: it sets ii to -25 and prints the absolute value 25. Then the derived constructor sets ll to -1000 and prints 1000. The 6 from Main is unused.

Output:

25
1000
